title: Give every import its own rejected-row count

blocks.text: A warehouse system imports supplier files and reports, for each file, how many rows failed validation. One `ImportAudit` serves the whole system, and several files can be imported at the same time on different threads. Rows arrive only through a callback: `RowSource.forEachRow` hands them one at a time to the action you pass it.
Write `rejected(source)` in `src/main/java/practice/ImportAudit.java`: the number of the file's rows that `check` doesn't accept.
When you're done, each file's report holds that file's count and nothing else, however many files were audited before it or alongside it. About four lines.

cases.says: one import's count is the number of its rows the check rejects
a second import audited by the same instance is counted from zero
when another import is audited while one is half read, each gets only its own rows' count

origin.section: State a Lambda Changes Through an Array or a Field Is Shared by Every Invocation

concepts: State a lambda reaches through a captured array or a field is shared by every invocation, and a field by every call of the method; a counter kept there adds across calls or is reset by a concurrent caller.
